title: How to check blood sugar with a meter
what: A glucose meter shows your blood sugar from one drop of blood from your finger. You can do it yourself at home.
why: For diabetes, to adjust treatment and to catch blood sugar that is too low or too high in time.
duration: about 1 to 2 minutes; the result shows in a few seconds
tell_doctor: How often and when you check your sugar
If you often have low readings
If the meter numbers do not match how you feel

prepare.title: Hands
prepare.text: Wash your hands with warm water and soap, and dry them well. Anything sweet on your fingers will change the result.

prepare.title: Test strips
prepare.text: Check the expiry date. Keep strips in a closed container, away from moisture and sunlight.

prepare.title: When to check
prepare.text: Your doctor will tell you how many times a day and when: before meals, after meals, or at bedtime.

bring: Your meter, test strips, and lancets
A log book or your phone for notes
steps: Put a test strip into the meter
Put a new lancet into the lancing device
Prick the side of your fingertip. It hurts less there
Gently massage the finger until a drop forms. Do not squeeze hard
Touch the strip to the drop. The meter draws in the blood by itself
After a few seconds, a number appears. Write it down with the time
feel: A quick prick in the finger
If you always prick the same spot, it can get sore. Switch fingers
after: Press a cotton pad to your finger
Throw away the lancet and strip
Show your log to your doctor at every visit
red_flags: Low sugar and you feel unwell, with shaking, sweating, or confusion: eat something sweet and check again
Very high sugar with strong thirst, vomiting, or drowsiness: call emergency services

faq.q: Why does my meter show a different number than the lab?
faq.a: A small difference is normal. If the difference is big, check your strips and ask your doctor.

faq.q: Do I need to wipe my finger with alcohol?
faq.a: Washing your hands is usually enough. If you used alcohol, let your finger dry first.

reminders.text: Time to check your blood sugar. Wash your hands, prick the side of your finger, and write down the result.
